methodology: Analytical sensitivity analysis varying key assumptions within biologically plausible ranges
note: Values are PREDICTED based on understanding of model structure, not from re-running experiments. Full computational sensitivity analysis would require 50+ simulation runs.

parameters.description: Shared signal weight α in latent factor model. Controls signal correlation across modalities.

0.0.interpretation: At α=0, modalities are independent → fusion provides ZERO benefit. GNN AUC would be ~0.52 (random).
0.0.claim_breakage: The 11.9% GNN improvement claim breaks at α=0. All fusion models collapse to random. The ENTIRE multi-modal fusion narrative depends on α > 0.

0.1.interpretation: Very weak correlation → minimal fusion benefit. GNN only marginally better than single modality.
0.1.claim_breakage: Fusion benefit is within noise range. Statistical significance unlikely.

0.3.claim_breakage: Already marginal — benefit may not be significant at n=90

0.5.interpretation: Strong correlation makes fusion clearly beneficial. However, ensemble with correlated detectors DEGRADES.
0.5.claim_breakage: Ensemble cost-savings claim may break at α > 0.5

0.7.interpretation: Very high correlation. Fusion improves but ensemble becomes counterproductive.
0.7.claim_breakage: Ensemble sensitivity gain becomes NEGATIVE. The ensemble + fusion approach becomes self-defeating.

parameters.real_world_concern: α is UNKNOWN at 0.001% ctDNA. No empirical measurement exists. If α < 0.1, multi-modal fusion provides negligible benefit.

parameters.description: Effective ctDNA genome equivalents per tumor cell (incorporates shedding + clearance + survival).

0.3x_baseline.interpretation: Lower shedding → slower signal rise → CET needs more measurements → some cancers fail to cross threshold in 730-day window.
0.3x_baseline.claim_breakage: 100% sensitivity claim breaks. CET still outperforms single-timepoint but not perfectly.

0.5x_baseline.interpretation: Moderate reduction. Most cancers still detected but later.

2x_baseline.interpretation: Higher shedding → faster detection. CET maintains perfect sensitivity.
2x_baseline.claim_breakage: No breakage but assumptions even more optimistic

parameters.real_world_concern: Effective ctDNA shedding rate varies 10-100× across tumor types. At the low end (e.g., gliomas), ctDNA-based screening may be impossible regardless of method.

parameters.description: Tumor doubling time in days (uniform 100-300 distribution in simulation).

100_days.interpretation: Fast-growing tumors detected very early. No sensitivity impact.
100_days.claim_breakage: Makes detection time claims more impressive

300_days.interpretation: Slow-growing tumors may not cross threshold within 730-day study window.
300_days.claim_breakage: 100% sensitivity claim breaks. ~8% of slow-growing tumors missed.

400_days.interpretation: Very slow growth → most tumors don't produce enough trajectory for CET.
400_days.claim_breakage: Sensitivity claim severely broken. CET advantage over single-timepoint largely disappears.

500_days.interpretation: Extremely indolent cancers. CET provides minimal benefit over single-timepoint.
500_days.claim_breakage: CET no longer clearly superior to single-timepoint screening

parameters.real_world_concern: Many screen-detected cancers (especially prostate, thyroid) have doubling times > 500 days. For these, quarterly CET screening may be ineffective.

parameters.description: Sequencing depth at each genomic position.

10000x.interpretation: At 10,000×, Poisson noise is 5× worse. Few mutant molecules captured. CET benefit severely diminished.
10000x.claim_breakage: 100% sensitivity claim broken. 1.55× improvement may drop to <1.2×. Cost-effectiveness argument collapses.

20000x.interpretation: Moderate depth. CET still works but with reduced performance.

100000x.interpretation: Even deeper sequencing. Better variant calling. CET remains at ceiling.
100000x.claim_breakage: No breakage but cost becomes even more prohibitive

parameters.real_world_concern: 50,000× across a broad panel costs $2000-5000. For POPULATION SCREENING (not high-risk surveillance), this is economically infeasible. The model's assumptions are for high-risk surveillance, not population screening.

5mL.interpretation: Half the genome equivalents → 2× worse Poisson noise. Significantly impacts sensitivity.
5mL.claim_breakage: 100% sensitivity claim broken at standard clinical draw volumes

8mL.interpretation: Standard clinical tube size. Moderate impact.

parameters.real_world_concern: Standard clinical tubes are 8-10mL. Real-world draws often yield 6-8mL after processing. The 10mL in simulation represents optimal conditions.

parameters.description: Fraction of patients with clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP).

5percent.interpretation: 5% CHIP prevalence (age ~50-60). Moderate false positive rate from CHIP mutations.
5percent.claim_breakage: 99.95% specificity claim broken. Real-world specificity much worse.

10percent.interpretation: 10% CHIP prevalence (age >60). CHIP mutations (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1) produce stable-but-elevated VAF signals.
10percent.claim_breakage: Specificity broken. PPV drops to near-zero. Population screening infeasible without CHIP filtering.

15percent.interpretation: 15% CHIP prevalence (age >70). Severe false positive problem.
15percent.claim_breakage: Complete failure of specificity claims. Requires matched WBC sequencing.

parameters.real_world_concern: CHIP is UNAVOIDABLE in any screening population aged >50. CET's streak/trend bonuses are partially robust to CHIP (stable signal → no rising trend → lower score), but the model hasn't tested this. This is the SINGLE BIGGEST THREAT to real-world specificity.

parameters.description: Amplitude of benign transient spikes (inflammation, infection).

2x_baseline.interpretation: Larger benign spikes more likely to trigger false detections.
2x_baseline.claim_breakage: Minor specificity impact — CET's streak bonus partially robust to single spikes

5x_baseline.interpretation: Very large benign spikes (e.g., severe infection, surgery) could trigger CET if consecutive.
5x_baseline.claim_breakage: Specificity significantly degraded if spike frequency is correlated with time

10x_baseline.interpretation: Extreme benign conditions (major surgery, sepsis) produce sustained trajectory-like signals.
10x_baseline.claim_breakage: Specificity claim broken for patients with severe intercurrent illness

parameters.real_world_concern: Real benign cfDNA spikes from surgery, trauma, or severe infection can reach 5-20× baseline and persist for weeks. Consecutive quarterly draws during such episodes could trigger false CET detections.

parameters.description: Multiplier on Poisson sampling noise (captures additional technical variation beyond pure Poisson).

2x.interpretation: Additional overdispersion from library prep, PCR bias, etc.

3x.interpretation: Realistic technical noise level for ultra-low input cfDNA libraries.
3x.claim_breakage: CET advantage over single-timepoint severely diminished

parameters.real_world_concern: Real cfDNA sequencing has overdispersion beyond Poisson (Negative Binomial with dispersion ~0.05-0.1). The pure Poisson model is optimistic.

key_findings: The CET 100% sensitivity claim is FRAGILE — it breaks under realistic perturbations to sequencing depth, blood volume, tumor doubling time, or ctDNA shedding rate
The GNN fusion benefit is PARAMETER-DEPENDENT — it disappears entirely if cross-modality correlation (α) approaches zero
CHIP (clonal hematopoiesis) is the SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT missing factor — not modeling CHIP is a critical omission for any ctDNA-based screening method
The 1.55× improvement is NOT a stable effect size — it varies from ~1.0× to 1.8× depending on parameter settings
At the very parameter values most likely in real-world screening (lower depth, smaller volume, slower-growing tumors), CET performance degrades toward single-timepoint levels
